current.text: Zubac is in Indiana's projected starting five with Haliburton, Nembhard, Nesmith and Siakam.
Jay Huff is the backup center. The depth behind Huff is weak (Larry Nance Jr. or Kobe Brown).
Minutes are the main concern. Rick Carlisle has a history of limiting starting center minutes, and Huff is a decent backup, so expect around 30 minutes.
He should be much better after a disappointing season, because he runs pick and roll with Tyrese Haliburton.
His fit is a question. He comes from a very slow Clippers team into an uptempo system that needs quicker decisions.
He missed time last season with a fractured rib and an ankle injury, and played only six games for Indiana after he arrived.
The fractured rib from last season is no concern at all.
Yahoo's rank of 57 is too aggressive for category leagues. His ESPN ADP of 95 is attractive. The expert ranks him 60 to 75 in category leagues.
He is the expert's best target on the Pacers, depending on the platform price.
In an auction mock, Josh would pay 11 or 12 USD for him and 14 USD at most. He went for 16 USD.
Indiana plays 3-4-3 games in our fantasy playoff weeks (season ending March 28), which is not ideal. The team has 15 back-to-backs.
Carlisle likes to keep minutes down and rest players on back-to-backs.
Indiana is projected to win 46 to 48 games.

durable.text: He is an elite rebounder and screener, and a strong post-up player.
High FG% on solid volume and big rebound numbers are his standout categories.
He almost never shoots threes, so he gives nothing in 3PM.
His steals are low for a center.
His minutes usually sit around 29 to 30. He played 33 minutes only once, and his production exploded that year.
His high 9-cat rank in his best season overstated his real value.

note: Zubac is a FG% and rebounds center with zero threes and few steals. That makes him a natural fit for punt 3PM builds, and his FT% (about 69% on under 3 attempts) does little damage. Yahoo values him at 18 USD and our league paid 20 USD last year, but ESPN has him at 4 USD and the experts rank him 60 to 75 in categories. Josh caps him at 14 USD after he went for 16 USD in a mock, so aim for about 10 to 14 USD. Early in the season, check whether Carlisle gives him more than 30 minutes or splits more time with Jay Huff, since his one 33-minute season was his big one.
